solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Liberal backing secures unionist party development

indicators.note: the reversed word holds the unionist letter firmly inside it
backing means the abbreviation for Liberal is read from the back

parts.note: the DUP is Northern Ireland's Democratic Unionist Party

explanation.surface: A political report: a Liberal backing deal props up a unionist party's growth.
explanation.walkthrough: The DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland, which fits the surface's unionist politics.
explanation.definitionFit: A build-up is a gradual growth or accumulation, so it is a kind of development.

clue.text: Bar, welcoming business in Kentish Town, provides breakfast fare

indicators.note: the word for bar takes the business abbreviation in, as a host lets a guest inside

parts.note: to bar is to BAN
CO is short for company, a business
Sandwich is a town in the English county of Kent

explanation.surface: A pub in Kentish Town, the London district, serves breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: Kentish Town is a district of north London, but here it means a town in Kent: Sandwich, an old port on the Kent coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Rashers of bacon between bread are a classic morning meal in British cafes.

clue.text: Bewildered by naiad sporting with Zeus? Not half!

indicators.note: sporting means playing about, so the letters are rearranged
not half keeps only the first two of the four letters

explanation.surface: A water nymph frolicking with the king of the gods is utterly confused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' sounds like an exclamation of agreement, but it halves ZEUS to ZE, rearranged with NAIAD.
explanation.definitionFit: In a daze means stunned and confused, unable to think clearly.

clue.text: Gets rid of politician involved in endless smut

indicators.note: the politician sits inside the shortened word for smut
the last letter of the word for smut is cut off

parts.note: smut is soot or dirt, so DUST
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A tabloid tale of an MP mixed up in an endless smut scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: Smut here is dust or grime, not lewd material.
explanation.definitionFit: To dump something is to throw it away or discard it.

clue.text: Tentatively plan writer abridging a bit of dialogue at the end of chapter one

indicators.note: the shortened dialogue piece comes after the chapter and one

parts.note: a pen is something you write with

indicators.note: abridging shortens the word for a bit of dialogue by its final letter

parts.note: a LINE is one speech in a script

explanation.surface: An author edits a line of dialogue at the close of chapter one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' is the pen, not the author the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: To pencil in an appointment is to arrange it provisionally, since pencil can be rubbed out.

clue.text: Teams of 4 kids chasing first spot

indicators.note: the quadruplets come after the opening letter, as if running behind it
first picks only the opening letter of spot

parts.note: the word spot supplies its initial letter
quads are four children born at one birth

explanation.surface: Four-player teams of children race to grab the first place.
explanation.walkthrough: Kids here are children born together: quadruplets, quads for short.
explanation.definitionFit: Squads are groups of players or people working as units.

clue.text: Washes medic's uniform

definitions.meaning: first meaning: cleans by rubbing hard
second meaning: the loose clothing worn by surgeons and hospital staff

explanation.walkthrough: One sense is a verb, the other a plural noun for hospital clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrubbing is hard cleaning; surgical scrubs are the garments worn in operating theatres.

clue.text: Unmoved, international organisation has conservative suspended

parts.note: the UN is the United Nations
hanged means hung up, suspended from a rope

explanation.surface: A world body has stood a Tory member down, unmoved by protest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suspended' suggests removal from office, but here it means hung from a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unchanged has not been altered or shifted, so it remains unmoved.

clue.text: Dead issue absorbing tabloid is going on too long

indicators.note: the pair for dead and issue take the tabloid into their middle

parts.note: issue means offspring, so a son
a rag is slang for a low-quality newspaper

explanation.surface: A stale story keeps running in the tabloid press long after it has died.
explanation.walkthrough: Issue is offspring, not a news topic.
explanation.definitionFit: When something drags on, it continues tediously beyond its natural end.

clue.text: Fossil fuel supplier and oilman offset carbon ahead of energy reading

indicators.note: the reworked letters come before energy and reading
offset suggests letters knocked out of position and set down in another order

parts.note: taken as written
R, one of the three Rs: reading, writing and arithmetic

explanation.surface: An oil executive offsets carbon emissions before an energy meter reading.
explanation.walkthrough: Carbon offsetting is a real practice, which hides that 'offset' signals an anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Coal is a fossil fuel, and the person who digs it out supplies it.

clue.text: Ringing family at weekend

parts.note: a clan is an extended family group
the end of the word week is its last letter, K

explanation.surface: The family phones each other at the weekend.
explanation.walkthrough: Weekend is read as the end of 'week', not Saturday and Sunday.
explanation.definitionFit: A clank is a loud metallic ringing sound, so the noun fits a ringing noise.

clue.text: Very eager to have newly unmasked star hosting episode's finale

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take in the last letter of the episode
newly means the letters are made anew in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the finale of a word is its closing letter

parts.note: the word episode, whose last letter is wanted

explanation.surface: A TV star unmasked in the final episode, as on a celebrity reveal show.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is an old simile: mustard is sharp, and keen once meant pungent.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone full of enthusiasm and eagerness.

clue.text: Comes close to crying heading off after final production

indicators.note: the shortened crying word comes after that letter
final picks the closing letter of production

parts.note: the word production, whose last letter is wanted

indicators.note: the word for crying loses its head, its first letter

parts.note: TEARS, the weeping itself

explanation.surface: An actor in tears heads off after the last night of a show.
explanation.definitionFit: To near something is to approach it or draw close.

clue.text: Setter defeated by computer technology?

parts.note: IT is information technology
beats means defeats, the active form of being defeated by
the setter refers to themselves as ME

explanation.surface: A crossword setter confesses to being beaten by computers.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a sentence, computer technology beats the setter; the phrase also means I am baffled.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is said when one is puzzled, which fits a setter outdone by machines.

clue.text: Drink's provided following weary Dad's return

indicators.note: the word for provided comes after the reversed part
the words for weary and Dad turn back, read right to left

parts.note: to tire is to grow weary
PA is a word for father
provided that means if

explanation.surface: A tired father comes home and needs a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperitif is an alcoholic drink taken before a meal to stimulate the appetite.

clue.text: Pressing hospital department to support organised sit-ins

indicators.note: in a down answer the department sits below, propping up the rest
organised means the protest letters are put into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
ENT is Ear, Nose and Throat

explanation.surface: Hospital staff support organised protests with sit-ins.
explanation.definitionFit: An insistent demand is urgent and persistent, which is what pressing means.

clue.text: Suitable for all to have one day on horseback in the country

indicators.note: on places one day after the reversed horse, in an across answer coming to its right

parts.note: U is the British film certificate for universal viewing
a horse is a NAG, and back reverses it
A is one, the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Everyone gets a day of pony trekking in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British film rating meaning suitable for all ages. Horseback is split into horse and back, the nag read backwards, with one day after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Uganda is a landlocked nation in East Africa.

clue.text: Happy going round Spain without a vehicle

indicators.note: the phrase meaning without a vehicle surrounds the letter for Spain

parts.note: car-free means having no car
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A cheerful traveller tours Spain with no car.
explanation.definitionFit: Carefree means free of worry, so untroubled and happy.

clue.text: Detective to take legal action about son's neglect

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector

indicators.note: the legal action word wraps round the letter for son

parts.note: to sue is to bring a court case

explanation.surface: A detective sues over neglect of his son.
explanation.definitionFit: Disuse is the state of no longer being used, a form of neglect.

clue.text: Stay very neutral describing day in Paris

indicators.note: describing in its sense of drawing round: very and neutral encircle the French day

parts.note: so means very, as in so good
jour is French for day

explanation.surface: A neutral account of a day spent in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Describing' is used in its geometric sense of tracing round, so it signals containment.
explanation.definitionFit: A sojourn is a temporary stay somewhere.

clue.text: Cruelly ready to puncture mother's reverie

indicators.note: the rearranged letters pierce into the word for mother

parts.note: a dam is a mother animal, used of horses

indicators.note: cruelly suggests letters treated roughly and thrown out of order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone cruelly ready to burst a mother's daydream bubble.
explanation.definitionFit: A daydream is a pleasant reverie or fantasy while awake.

clue.text: Put in charge of sorting out unrest overwhelming Thailand

indicators.note: the rearranged letters engulf the letter for Thailand
sorting out means putting the unrest letters into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
T is the international vehicle code for Thailand

explanation.surface: Authorities tackle unrest that is overwhelming Thailand.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrust someone with a task is to give them responsibility for it.

clue.text: Quickly hiding money in trash, turned up largely cleaned out

indicators.note: in a down answer, turned up means read from bottom to top
the bin holds the money letter out of sight

parts.note: a bin is where you put trash; to bin is to trash

indicators.note: the inside of largely is emptied, leaving its first and last letters

parts.note: the word largely, of which only the outer letters survive

explanation.surface: Someone quickly hides cash in the rubbish, which turned up mostly emptied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Largely' looks like it means mostly, but it is the fodder, emptied of its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: To move nimbly is to move with quick, light agility.

clue.text: Representing Iceni over-simply is wrong

indicators.note: the rearranged tribe's letters are placed over, covering, the word for simply
representing in the sense of re-presenting: the tribe's letters shown in a new form

parts.note: taken as written
just means simply, as in just wonderful

explanation.surface: A historian depicting the Iceni, Boudicca's tribe, too simply gets it wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: The Iceni were the ancient British tribe led by Boudicca.
explanation.definitionFit: An injustice is a wrong, an unfair act done to someone.

clue.text: Stings best treated without iodine

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the reworked letters enclose iodine
treated means the letters are processed into another arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
I is the chemical symbol for iodine

explanation.surface: Insect stings are best treated without iodine antiseptic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' here means outside, not lacking, so the iodine goes in rather than out.
explanation.definitionFit: Insect bites and stings are both small wounds from a creature's attack.

clue.text: Irregular verb answer's put in bold

indicators.note: the letter for answer is placed inside the rearranged letters
irregular means the letters of verb are out of their usual order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A grammar note: an irregular verb's answer is printed in bold type.
explanation.walkthrough: Bold looks like a typeface instruction, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Brave and bold are synonyms for courageous.

clue.text: Tube's outside university accommodation

indicators.note: the tube word sits outside, wrapping round the university letter

parts.note: a hose is a flexible tube

explanation.surface: A student's lodging sits just outside the university Tube station.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tube is the London Underground, but here it is just a pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A house provides accommodation, a place to live.

clue.text: Scottish island copper finally arrested a big fish

parts.note: Barra is an island in the Outer Hebrides
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of arrested

parts.note: the word arrested, whose last letter is wanted
taken as written

explanation.surface: On a Scottish island, a policeman finally arrests a big shot.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper suggests a police officer, but it is the metal. Big fish also means an important criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: The barracuda is a large predatory sea fish with sharp teeth.

clue.text: Difficult for seabird having tiny wings

indicators.note: the bird has the wing letters attached after it

parts.note: the knot is a wading shorebird

indicators.note: the wings of a word are its outside letters, first and last

parts.note: the word tiny, whose outer letters are its wings

explanation.surface: Life is hard for a seabird with tiny wings.
explanation.definitionFit: A knotty problem is a complicated one, hard to untangle.

clue.text: Applied to have old tree chopped down

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: chopped means the tree is cut up and its letters rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
D is short for down, as in crossword clue references

explanation.surface: Force was used to have an old tree chopped down.
explanation.definitionFit: Exerted means brought to bear, as force or influence is applied.
